content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text counts listed verses toward a broken challenger link, which is the conduct K-G4 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost\" and Matthew 1:25 \"knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.","room":"The phrase 'counts toward a broken link is counted this way' could mean either all verses listed in a broken-link entry must satisfy K-G4, or only verses expressly labeled as unanswered witnesses must; I read it as covering the verses this judge lists as supporting the broken link.","why":"The text lists Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:25, and Luke 1:34 as support for a broken link but neither quotes an earlier-round sentence pressing them against that link nor names a round, so the counted verses do not meet K-G4."}
